output.answer: NBCUniversal is organized into four business groups — Media, Studios, NBC News Group, and Destinations & Experiences. Its principal subsidiaries include the NBC broadcast network and owned stations, Telemundo (and Universo), Bravo, NBC Sports, NBC News, the Peacock and Hayu streaming services, the Universal film and TV studios (Universal Pictures with Focus Features, Illumination and DreamWorks Animation; Universal Studio Group with Universal Television, UCP and Universal Television Alternative Studio), and Universal Destinations & Experiences' theme parks (Universal Orlando, Universal Studios Hollywood, Universal Studios Japan, Universal Beijing Resort, Universal Studios Singapore, plus new ventures in Las Vegas, a kids resort in 2026 and a planned UK resort). Note two recent changes: the cable networks (CNBC, MS NOW/MSNBC, USA Network, Syfy, E!, Golf Channel, Oxygen) were spun off into Versant, completed January 2, 2026, so they are no longer NBCUniversal subsidiaries; and on June 29, 2026 Comcast announced plans to spin off NBCUniversal — whose portfolio will then include Sky — into an independent public company expected to complete around 2027.
caveats: Several lists of NBCUniversal subsidiaries still name the US cable networks (CNBC, MSNBC/MS NOW, USA Network, Syfy, E!, Oxygen, Golf Channel); these were spun off into Versant, with the spin-off completed January 2, 2026, so they are no longer NBCUniversal assets.

Sky is not currently an NBCUniversal subsidiary — it is a separate Comcast business — but Comcast's June 29, 2026 announcement says NBCUniversal's global portfolio will include Sky once the planned spin-off of NBCUniversal from Comcast (expected in about a year, i.e. ~2027) is completed.

The most granular subsidiary-by-subsidiary enumeration (stations, joint ventures, international channels) comes from a Wikipedia asset list, a third-party source; NBCUniversal's own pages list brands and divisions but not every legal entity, so exact corporate structures (joint-venture percentages, minor units) may differ or change.

output.question: What are NBCUniversal's subsidiaries?

key_facts.fact: NBCUniversal organizes its businesses into four divisions: Media, NBC News Group, Studios, and Destinations & Experiences.

NBCUniversal's brands/subsidiaries include NBC, NBC News, NBC News NOW, NBC Olympics, NBC Sports, NBCSN, NBCUniversal Local, Telemundo, Bravo, Peacock, Hayu, Universal Pictures, Universal Pictures Content Group, Universal Pictures Home Entertainment, Universal Pictures International, Focus Features, Illumination, DreamWorks, Universal Studio Group (housing Universal Television, UCP and Universal Television Alternative Studio), Universal Products & Experiences, and the Universal parks and resorts (Universal Orlando Resort, Universal Studios Hollywood, Universal Studios Japan, Universal Beijing Resort, Universal Studios Singapore, Universal Horror Unleashed, Universal Kids Resort, Universal United Kingdom Resort).

Per a detailed asset list, NBCUniversal's holdings also include Universal Filmed Entertainment Group units (Working Title Films, United International Pictures, minority stakes in Amblin Partners and Blumhouse), Universal Television and Universal Global Television labels (Carnival Films, Heyday Television, Lark Productions, NBCUniversal Formats), Telemundo Enterprises (Telemundo, Universo, Telemundo Studios), NBCUniversal International Networks (Universal TV, DreamWorks Channel, Studio Universal, 13th Street, Diva, Telemundo Internacional), Peacock, NBC News, NBC owned stations and Telemundo Station Group, plus minority JVs (MLB Network 5.44%, NHL Network 15.6%, SNY 8%).

Versant — the spin-off of NBCUniversal's cable network assets (CNBC, MS NOW/MSNBC, USA Network, Syfy, E!, Golf Channel, Oxygen) — was completed on January 2, 2026 and is no longer part of NBCUniversal.

Comcast announced on June 29, 2026 its intention to spin off NBCUniversal (whose portfolio will include Sky) into an independent publicly traded company, expected to complete in approximately one year (~2027); NBCUniversal is currently a wholly owned subsidiary of Comcast.

In its SEC filings, Comcast describes NBCUniversal's segments: Media (NBC and Telemundo broadcast networks, owned local stations, Peacock, national cable networks and international networks including Sky Sports networks in the UK and Italy), Studios (NBCUniversal and Sky film and TV studio production/distribution), and Destinations & Experiences (theme parks); NBCUniversal Media, LLC's sole member is NBCUniversal, LLC.
